memories.memory: I support Indigenous self-government and believe public agencies should transfer real decision-making power, not just consult communities after policies are already written.
During the 2024 election, I volunteered about 30 hours for a local candidate who wanted to replace mandatory minimum sentences with community-based programs.
I am politically opposed to expanding police budgets without independent oversight, even though several people in my department think that position is impractical.

I believe government employees should be allowed to refuse directives that clearly violate civil rights, and I would accept disciplinary action rather than sign off on something I considered unlawful.
My political views became much more distrustful after a regional housing program in 2022 spent roughly $180,000 on consultants while leaving several families without placements.
I do not follow an organized religion, and I generally view moral decisions as matters of responsibility and consequences rather than divine rules.
I support strong public-sector unions and progressive taxation, but I would still vote for a candidate who opposed my economic views if I thought they were more competent and less corrupt.
